Ledger header truncation stats verified exactly (608 ellipsis-marked, 126 intact, 515 at exactly 220 chars, single 539-char row at 11.01.02). Index Must-by-domain table and per-domain children counts reconcile exactly with the ledger and with disk. scoringNote: Dimensions applicable to this unit: 1 Problem Clarity (OK), 3 Feature Completeness (OK - MoSCoW exact, mutually exclusive, disk-verified), 7 Open Question Resolution (WARN), 8 Structural Compliance (WARN), plus one implementer-simulation forced-invention item scored as a full point. Dimensions 2/4/5/6 are N/A: personas, constraints, success metrics and competitive positioning are authored in meta/*.md and ../vision.md, which are separate audit units; the root files only cite them, and a cross-reference carrying the detail is not a finding. ambiguity% = 2.0 / 5 = 40%.

findings.forcedInvention: Who owns the follow/save/watchlist primitive, the promoted-placement/advertising-disclosure mechanism, the referral/invite/affiliate system, the role-aware onboarding/activation flow, offline field capture, and accessibility - each is either a shared cross-cut, a per-domain feature rebuilt N times, or out of scope. The vision layer answers none of the three.
findings.claim: Six cross-cutting systems that domain-map-proposal.md carries as ratified, named, product-affecting cross-cuts with explicit affected-domain lists are absent from the consolidated 25-mechanism registry in ideation-cx.md, absent from its Section 1b unratified-candidate table, and absent from the not-product routing table. They vanish between two root documents with no merge note, no owner, no routing target and no tracked question.
findings.evidence: domain-map-proposal.md:366 '| Promoted Placement & Advertising | Governed paid discovery, sponsorship, and advertising disclosure. | 13 Gear; 14 Digital Goods; 05 Services; 04 Opportunities; 20 Fanbase; 21 Promotion; 03 Community. |'; :367 '| Referrals, Invites & Affiliates | Invitation, attribution, incentive, and abuse-controlled referral system. | 01 Identity; 03 Community; 13 Gear; 14 Digital Goods; 05 Services; 20 Fanbase. |'; :369 '| Follow, Save & Watchlist | Shared intentional-interest, collection, and alert primitives. | 03 Community; 04 Opportunities; 13 Gear; 14 Digital Goods; 11 Licensing; 20 Fanbase; 16 Venues/Studios/Spaces. |'; :356 '| Onboarding & Role-Aware Activation | Role-specific progressive activation and first-value journeys. | 01 Identity; 02 Credits; 05 Services; 13 Gear; 14 Digital Goods; 16 Venues/Studios/Spaces; 17 Live Booking; 20 Fanbase. |'; :362 '| Accessibility | Accessible component, content, and critical-flow behavior. | 01 Identity; 13 Gear; 07 Music Projects; 20 Fanbase; 19 Ticketing; 16 Venues/Studios/Spaces; 06 Education. |'; :373 '| Offline & Low-Connectivity Field Resilience | Offline capture, synchronization, and degraded field workflows. | 18 Show Production; 19 Ticketing; 02 Credits; 15 Gear Registry; 17 Live Booking. |'. domain-map-proposal.md:440 '**Status: [RATIFIED - owner reaffirmed the 24-domain classification on 2026-07-19; existing fractal domain tree is authoritative]**'. Against ideation-cx.md:15-41, the 25-row registry, which contains no row for any of the six (machine-checked: 'advertis' appears once in the whole file, inside an unrelated 08-16 interaction row; 'referral' once, inside an unrelated 03-04 row; 'watchlist', 'affiliate', 'sponsor', 'offline' appear zero times; 'onboard' only inside the Payments row's 'KYC/KYB onboarding'; 'accessib' only inside an unrelated 18-19 row). ideation-cx.md:45 states the tracking mechanism these six are missing from and names the exact failure mode: 'Shared-mechanism candidates surfaced by cross-pair synthesis but NOT yet promoted into the Section 1 registry. Each carries a deciding question and a target stage. Downstream (`/create-prd`) MUST rule on promotion before any owning domain builds a private copy - the failure mode is each domain rebuilding a subtly incompatible version.' - and that table (ideation-cx.md:49-50) holds only two candidates, Timestamped Annotation and Practice-Room Tools, neither of them one of the six. domain-map-proposal.md:379-402, the not-product routing table, routes 24 concerns downstream and routes none of the six.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building domain 04 Opportunities and domain 13 Gear Marketplace both need 'save this for later' and alerting. Nothing in the vision layer says these are one primitive, so 04 builds a saved-opportunity table and 13 builds a watchlist table with different alert semantics and different privacy scoping - exactly the outcome ideation-cx.md:45 says the candidate table exists to prevent. Worse for Promoted Placement & Advertising: it spans 7 domains and carries a statutory disclosure obligation, and with no owner named, either every marketplace domain invents its own ad-disclosure rule or the capability is silently dropped from a product whose domain map ratified it.

findings.claim: ideation-cx.md's own Section 3 synthesis names a third shared-mechanism candidate and states in terms that it is tracked nowhere - yet it was not added to the Section 1b candidate table that exists for exactly this purpose, and it carries no owner and no target stage.
findings.evidence: ideation-cx.md:398 (pair 02-11, Credits x Music Licensing) '...Shared-primitive candidate: `cited, not claimed` verification could be one mechanism across credits (02) and third-party licence verification (11.08.03) - a strong candidate for one shared mechanism rather than two, and it is in neither the Section 1 registry nor the Section 1b candidate list, so nothing currently stops both domains building it twice.' Compare ideation-cx.md:47-50, the Section 1b table, whose columns are '| Candidate | Provisional owner | Serves | Deciding question | Target stage |' and which contains exactly two rows (Timestamped Annotation, Practice-Room Tools) - neither is this one. No owner, no deciding-question row, no target stage anywhere for 'cited, not claimed'.
findings.failure_scenario: The Section 1b preamble says `/create-prd` MUST rule on promotion for every candidate in that table before an owning domain builds a private copy. Because this candidate is not in the table, `/create-prd` has nothing to rule on, and domain 02 and domain 11 each ship their own verification mechanic - the precise duplication the sentence predicts, with no gate anywhere in the pipeline set to catch it.

findings.forcedInvention: Which domains consume the Realtime Rooms / Presence / Audio Transport cross-cut. Three root-level statements give three different sets; an implementer must pick one.
findings.claim: The consumer set for the 'Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport' cross-cut differs across three root-level statements, with no supersession marker on any of them. Domain 05 Services is named as a consumer by the ratifying decision and by the domain map but is absent from the registry row; 20 Fanbase is named by the domain map only; 17 and 18 are named by the registry only.
findings.evidence: ideation-index.md:201 (D-15) 'Audio transport extracted into the `Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport` cross-cut (serves Education, Services, Projects, Community)' - i.e. 06, 05, 07, 03. domain-map-proposal.md:352 '| Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport | Reusable synchronous room, presence, transport, routing, and capture primitive. | 08 Real-Time Jamming; 06 Education; 05 Services; 07 Music Projects; 03 Community; 20 Fanbase. |' - i.e. 08, 06, 05, 07, 03, 20. ideation-cx.md:31 '| **Realtime Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport** | 08 | 03,06,07,08,17,18 | Low-latency realtime rooms with presence, collaborative-editing state, and synchronized audio/media transport for jamming and remote sessions.' - i.e. 03, 06, 07, 08, 17, 18. Union minus intersection: 05 in two of three, 20 in one of three, 17 and 18 in one of three.
findings.failure_scenario: Domain 05 Services Marketplace has a 'Remote Session Performance' sub-domain (domain-map-proposal.md:106). Reading the registry row, which is the file the index designates as the consolidated cross-cut registry, an implementer concludes 05 is not a consumer and builds remote-session delivery without the shared room primitive - directly against D-15, the decision that created the cross-cut. Conversely an implementer reading D-15 provisions nothing for 17 and 18.

findings.claim: moscow-ledger.md's header restates the half of D-20 that D-31 superseded, with no supersession marker, and it contradicts the index's explicit statement that beachhead sequencing is no longer `/plan-phase`'s job.
findings.evidence: moscow-ledger.md:4 '> **Owner decision (D-20)**: all 195 Must-haves retained; sequencing deferred to `/plan-phase`.' Against ideation-index.md:206 (D-20) '**All 195 Must-haves retained** (still live). ~~v1 beachhead sequencing deferred to `/plan-phase`~~ **- the "defer the beachhead" half is AMENDED by D-31**, which chose v1 = session spine + v1.5 = marketplaces. The retention of all 195 Musts stands; only the sequencing-deferral is superseded.' And ideation-index.md:318-320 '**What `/plan-phase` does now**: it orders **within each release** by dependency. The beachhead is chosen (v1 = the spine); `/plan-phase` sequences the ~45 v1 Musts, then the ~26 v1.5 Musts. It no longer needs to pick a beachhead - D-31 did.' The ledger carries no strikethrough, no amendment note, and no reference to D-31 anywhere in the file.
findings.failure_scenario: `/plan-phase` opens the MoSCoW ledger - the document that actually holds all 734 tiered rows and is the natural input for sequencing - reads line 4, and treats beachhead selection as an open decision it must make. It re-derives a v1 scope from tier alone (195 Musts across 24 domains) rather than consuming D-31's ratified v1 = 01/02/05/07/09-capture ~45 Musts, producing a release plan the owner already rejected as over-aggressive under D-29.

findings.claim: The Progress Summary's file-inventory row is factually wrong on disk: it places moscow-ledger.md one directory level up when it is a root-level ideation file, it omits domain-map-proposal.md from the inventory entirely, and its 1,121 total double-counts ideation-index.md while the true count of .md files under ideation/ is 1,122.
findings.evidence: ideation-index.md:62 '| Total ideation files | **1,121** (734 features - 190 indexes - 190 CX - 6 meta - 1 super-index (`ideation-index.md`) - not counted: `../vision.md`, `../feature-ledger.md`, `../moscow-ledger.md` live one level up). ...' Disk truth (machine-checked): total .md under .memory/wiki/specs/ideation/ = 1,122; 190 *-index.md (= 24 domain + 165 sub-domain + ideation-index.md itself, so the '190 indexes' figure already contains the '1 super-index' added again); 190 *-cx.md; 6 meta; 734 leaves; root-level extras domain-map-proposal.md and moscow-ledger.md. `fs.existsSync('.../ideation/moscow-ledger.md')` = true; `fs.existsSync('.../specs/moscow-ledger.md')` = false. The same index links it as a sibling three sections later - ideation-index.md:265 '> **Full ledger with all 734 features, paths and rationale**: [moscow-ledger.md](./moscow-ledger.md)' - so the two statements about where the ledger lives cannot both hold. (vision.md and feature-ledger.md are correctly one level up.)
findings.failure_scenario: A downstream workflow told by the pipeline key file that the MoSCoW ledger lives one level up resolves `../moscow-ledger.md` and gets ENOENT, then either fails or proceeds without the only document that holds all 734 tier assignments. Separately, any agent reconciling counts from disk against this row finds a 1-file discrepancy and has no way to tell whether a file was lost or the row was never right.

findings.claim: Two root files state the cross-domain connectivity ratio differently - 211/276 versus 206/276 - using the same metric name and the same denominator, with no marker on either, and the index itself carries both numbers.
findings.evidence: ideation-index.md:212 (D-26) '**D-17 resolved - keep 24 domains.** Cross-domain connectivity is 211/276 pairs (76%) but judged **structural, not over-splitting**...'. Against ideation-cx.md:428 'A 24-domain graph has 276 possible unordered domain pairs. This map records **206 live interactions** - roughly 75% of the theoretical maximum - of which 184 carry real cross-domain synthesis and 22 are density-confirmed pending write-up.' and ideation-cx.md:429 '**D-17 verdict: STRUCTURAL, not over-split.** A connectivity of 206/276 (~75%) is high...'. The index's own Progress Summary agrees with 206, not 211 - ideation-index.md:76 '| Cross-domain interaction pairs synthesized | **206** (184 full synthesis, 22 tracked) - Step 6 complete |'. Machine count of the Section 2 interaction map: 206 data rows, 206 unique pairs, confidence distribution high 111 / medium 66 / medium-pending 11 / low 7 / low-pending 11, i.e. 184 synthesized + 22 pending - so 206 is the disk-true figure and D-26's 211 matches nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: D-26 is the decision that closed D-17's live hypothesis of domain-count inflation, and its stated evidence is the 211 figure. Anyone re-testing that hypothesis in `/create-prd` or `/decompose-architecture` recomputes 206 from the map, cannot reproduce 211, and cannot tell whether five pairs were dropped after the analysis (in which case the ratified conclusion rests on evidence that no longer exists) or whether the number was simply mistyped.

findings.claim: D-75's open question carries an owner marker but no deferral target, and the derived rule it ships alongside carries neither an owner nor a target - while the index's own rubric self-check asserts that every open question has both.
findings.evidence: ideation-index.md:260 (D-75) 'Tracked, unresolved - **[OWNER]**: are the five domains identical to domain 17\'s ratified work-type enum, or a fourth vocabulary? `01.03.02`:25 lists **sync** as publishing\'s *sibling* while `09.01.04`:102 carves sync *inside* publishing as a right type (performance, mechanical, sync, print); this needs a taxonomy ruling and is not answered here.' - no pipeline stage, no deadline, and no statement of what it blocks. Same decision, same paragraph: 'Derived rule (agent decision, owner may override): a representation edge must declare **at least one** domain at creation' - no owner assigned to the override and no stage by which it must be confirmed; the rule is restated verbatim into the ratified registry at ideation-cx.md:27 '(**derived rule - agent decision, owner may override**)', again with no owner or target. Against ideation-index.md:158 '| 7 | Open Question Resolution | OK | Every open question has owner + target stage (pipeline-stage = deadline). [vision.md](../vision.md) Open Questions |'. Contrast the well-formed pattern the same unit demonstrates elsewhere: moscow-ledger.md:790 gives Q-01 both an owner cell '**[OWNER]**' and a Deferred To cell '`/plan-phase` - the first consumer that reads tier and rationale together'; ideation-cx.md:47 gives every Section 1b candidate a 'Target stage' column.
findings.failure_scenario: The five `domains` values are literal in D-75, so an implementer can build the enum - but nothing says when the taxonomy ruling is due, so `/create-prd` and `/write-be-spec` both pass without resolving it. Domain 17's work-type enum and this five-value set are then modelled as two independent vocabularies, and the sync-is-a-sibling versus sync-is-inside-publishing conflict D-75 names is inherited into the schema, where fixing it becomes a migration rather than an ideation edit.

findings.claim: D-73 records an unresolved precondition it labels blocking, with no owner, no deferral target and no tracked question id anywhere - the only such self-declared blocker in the decision log.
findings.evidence: ideation-index.md:258 (D-73) '**Unresolved precondition, blocking a real population**: `15.07` publishes ORG registers, so per `16.03.02` DT-12 a sole-trader rehearsal Operator with no org entity cannot publish at all.' No `[OWNER]`, no `[PENDING - <stage>]`, no `[DEFERRED]`, no Q-id, and no routing to a downstream workflow. Compare how the adjacent decisions handle the same situation: ideation-index.md:255 (D-70) 'Nobody is assigned to gather the evidence - flagged as `vision.md` Q-07.' and ideation-index.md:256 (D-71) '**Explicitly does NOT close** nine other non-persona actors ... rolled up as `vision.md` Q-09.' - both route the unowned item to a tracked question; D-73 routes nowhere.
findings.failure_scenario: The gap is a hard functional exclusion, not a refinement: on the ratified model a sole-trader rehearsal-room operator cannot list a room at all, which silently removes a whole supply-side population from domain 16. Because it is recorded only as prose inside a decision body with no owner and no stage, no downstream gate will surface it, and `/create-prd` and `/write-architecture-spec` will both design domain 16's publishing flow around an org-only assumption that the decision itself flags as wrong.
